maria: Heads-up: follow-up on reassembly backpressure we observed in staging. short thread with concrete guards + long-term options.
Ajay: saw the spike at 14:22 where reassembly_miss_rate jumped to 2.3% and ingest queue latency doubled. what timeline do we want for an auto-protect?
Kai: problem summary: reassembly cache misses -> more opaque fallbacks -> larger payloads -> higher CPU+IO -> more queueing -> cascade. need a fast circuit to break the loop.
Sophia: proposed short-term guard: auto-enable "opaque-fallback-mode" per-shard when both conditions met for 1m: 1) reassembly_miss_rate > 0.75% and 2) ingest_queue_p50_latency > 200ms. revert only after 10m stable below thresholds.
Ajay: agrees but we should measure billing impact. add check: if opaque-mode increases billing_delta_ratio > 0.2% for a shard over 1h, notify finance and maintain manual override.
maria: draft SnQL to compute the trigger window:
``
SELECT shard, avg(reassembly_miss_rate) as miss, p50(ingest_queue_latency) as qlat FROM shard_ingest_metrics WHERE ts >= now()-1m GROUP BY shard HAVING miss>0.0075 AND qlat>200
```
if this returns rows, set opaque-fallback on those shards.
Kai: implementation note: opaque-fallback should be idempotent and cheap: set an ingest shard flag that makes it reject delta-only fragments with 409 -> edge will fall back to full envelope. that avoids expensive rehydration work.
Sophia: dashboard additions: per-shard reassembly_miss_rate (1m/5m), ingest_queue_p50/p95, bytes_per_request_95th, opaque_mode_active boolean. alert: any shard with opaque_mode_active and billing_delta_ratio>0.2% -> page finance oncall.
Ajay: Add a safety hysteresis: require 3 consecutive 1m windows matching conditions before flipping to opaque to avoid flapping on noise. Also exponential backoff on auto-revert (10m, 30m, 2h).
maria: long-term options we debated: 1) move rehydration to an async stream worker with backpressure tokens (complex but isolates hot path); 2) push more work to edge: allow edge to emit a small reassembly-proof summary that the ingest can cheaply check (requires edge change); 3) hybrid: keep delta envelopes but force periodic full checkpoints every N fragments (N=8) so rehydration never needs arbitrarily long sequences. thoughts?
Kai: (1) is safest for ingest but high infra cost. (2) is ideal but requires coordinated rollout. (3) is middle ground and probably lowest risk. simulations show checkpoints every 8 fragments reduce worst-case reassembly window from 60s to ~8s in practice.
Ajay: finance question: how to bill partial/ambiguous attributions during throttle events? finance-bot: If opaque_fallback is enabled, billing follows full-envelope path so attribution stays stable; ambiguous_attribution_count increments only when bloom/tombstone uncertain. We mark those customers as "best_effort" in daily reconcile.
Sophia: add telemetry for ambiguous_attribution_count and ambiguous_billing_revenue_estimate - both daily aggregates. we should alert if ambiguous_revenue_estimate > $50/day for canary customers.
ops-bot: infra-bot: enacted canary guard - opaque-fallback auto-toggle will be enabled in staging at 2026-03-24T02:00Z for testing.
maria: action items: Kai - implement auto-toggle + hysteresis (PR by EOD tomorrow). Ajay - add SnQL monitor + finance notification runbook. Sophia - dashboard tiles + alert thresholds. me - update RFC with checkpoint option and async rehydration pros/cons.
Ajay: one more: add metric reassembly_eviction_rate (evictions/sec). high eviction rate is precursor to cascade. use that as early-warning on the dashboard.
Kai: noted - i'll tune LRU sizes to keep eviction_rate<100/s per shard under 95th percentile load in sim.
maria: if we get no objections, i'll wire the small PR to add the SnQL monitor and the per-shard flag. targeting staging test tomorrow.
Sophia: +1. will prep playbook text: how to interpret opaque-fallback incidents and steps to unwind.
Ajay: +1. keep the auto-rollback conservative; prefer manual override if finance impact unclear.
Notes: keep follow-ups short; prefer numeric thresholds in alerts; plan for conservative defaults to avoid billing regressions.
